title: With Dejounte Murray trade request hovering, Pelicans’ Mosley sympathizes with frustrated fans
content:
Amid the drama of Dejounte Murray’s trade request and the harsh reality of a five-game losing streak, New Orleans Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley said he sympathizes with frustrated fans.

“I’m disappointed by how we’ve played and that the fans are looking at it like this is not what they’re expecting,” Mosley told reporters Friday night after his team’s 142-111 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies. “I understand that. I’m not ducking that. I’m not shying away from it.”

The Pelicans have lost their last three games by an average of 38.7 points. Their defense, which has fallen to 29th place in efficiency, has allowed at least 138 points in each of the last four games.

During this stretch, the fans haven’t been alone in experiencing frustration. The Pelicans announced Friday that Murray has requested a trade. After a 145-111 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday, Zion Williamson delivered a passionate speech about how each person in the locker room needed to look in the mirror. He called the performance against Brooklyn “unacceptable.”

Two days later, the Pelicans suffered another extremely lopsided loss at home and fell to 4-9 on the season.

“I know what we said, how we wanted to play, the product we wanted to put on the floor,” Mosley said. “And you saw it (during) that stretch of the early (hard-fought losses) and you saw it when we won four in a row. So it’s there. And that’s what we have to understand. This is a process. We’ll keep talking about that in some form or fashion. But just like the NBA, there’s highs, there’s lows. We’re going to find that stride because these guys’ energy and spirit was right. Now we just have to put the pieces together. And that’s on me as a coach to figure out the ways to put these guys in the best position to be successful.”

Including Murray, the Pelicans were without three opening-night starters Friday, with Trey Murphy III (knee) and Yves Missi (knee) sidelined by injuries.

Mosley, in his first season with the Pelicans, suggested he will consider defensive changes.

“I’m not happy,” Mosely said. “But not being happy doesn’t solve the problem. So there’s probably some adjustments that need to be made the way we’re guarding or not, lack thereof. And that’s part of on the coaching, what I’ve gotta do there, what we’ve gotta do there.

“There’s a will, there’s a want, there’s a desire, there’s rotations, there’s not straight-line drives, there’s not blow bys. The want to sit down and guard, but then also, if you do get beat, gotta have help. Those are a lot of situations. Now they shot the brakes out of the basketball, some highly contested ones, some wide-open ones because they did a great job reading the defense. But we’ve gotta be better there. And we will be.”

In a statement acknowledging Murray’s trade request, the Pelicans said Friday they will “evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization.” To avoid allowing the situation to become a distraction, Saddiq Bey said, the Pelicans need to “just keep the main thing, the main thing.”

“You’ve gotta focus on the task at hand,” Bey told reporters. “We’ve got a game tomorrow at 6 o’clock, and I’m trying to focus on trying to get a win.”

Bey indicated Murray’s trade request will not impact their relationship.

“It’s a business,” Bey said. “Obviously, we love him. I personally love him. I’ve known him for years. And it’s a business. There’s kind of some of those things I can’t really talk about or disclose, but we’re brothers for life.”

Mosely’s Pelicans have another test Saturday as they host the Denver Nuggets.

“That’s on me as a coach to figure out the ways to put these guys in the best position to be successful,” the coach said. “But yeah, if I’m the fans, I’m looking at it like there needs to be better. And we will be better.”
